question: In a Walmart SE-III round for a React + Kotlin Spring Boot role, the interviewer asked about authorization in the application: what the authorization methods are (the candidate named JWT, sessions and OAuth). Then: how do you handle local and global exceptions in your application, and write code to catch them (controller throwing exceptions, controller advice, exception handlers, custom exceptions)? Follow-up on custom exceptions (RuntimeException vs Exception): how do you always ensure that every exception returns a standard error code and message, for example code 123 meaning "user not found"?
lookingFor: Layered exception handling in Spring: local handlers and global advice
A systematic design where an error code is part of the exception contract
Safe fallback so unexpected exceptions never leak stack traces
Understanding of checked vs unchecked exceptions
Distinguishing authentication from authorization and comparing JWT, sessions, OAuth
followUps: Why does Spring roll back on RuntimeException but not on checked exceptions by default?
How would you propagate error codes across microservices?
How do you revoke a JWT before it expires?
What should an error response never contain?
